title: ORGANIC MATERIALS USED IN LAUNCHERS APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To establish a de-risking strategy for the non-European dependency for organic materials such as silicones,elastomers, glues, resins for thermal protections for launchers applications.Description:In 2025, European chemistry faces critical challenges due to structural crises, industrial site closures, andintense international competition. Many groups in Europe and outside of Europe are reorganizing theirproduction, closing plants, or relocating to more competitive regions like Asia. Between 2019 and 2023,Europe's chemical production fell by 12%, with closure of over 20 industrial sites. In addition, groups must faceevolutions of regulations (e.g. REACH), monitoring and anticipating future forbidden substances (Substancesof Very High Concern - SVHC) and focus newinvestments on green chemistry and decarbonization viabiosourced molecules, recycling, and carbon capture. For example, PFAS regulation will be effective at leastby end of 2028, and a huge number of products will be forbidden, and aeronautic and aerospace sectors willbe severely impacted. For silicones some non-European suppliers informed that a supply risk exists for someolder references.The qualification of these applications is long and complex. Silicones are used in componentsin the manufacture of thermal protection to contribute for maintaining the shape and the flexibility of the thermalprotection. They also allow to stick and join components, respecting the thermal sealing.Other materials / use cases in the scope of this activity include:- Elastomers: Used in solidengines as a gas protection Procured outside Europe- Glues and Thread lock: Many parts of launcher, from structural materials to-Thread locks, need specific glues.- Resins: Solid Rocket Motor parts are manufactured using resin (bearing reinforcement material or the RTMinjection moulding process).- Aluminium adhesives: Used to maintain an electrically grounded connection of the thermal protections inESR (Thermal Protection, Thermal Cap Capture System, Mechanical Anti-Pitching System and RodThermal Protection).Thisactivity aims at implementing and supporting when required a multi-sourcing strategy withphysicochemical characterizations of proposedalternatives.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Assessment of requirements available from European launcher manufacturers,- Analysis of supply resilience and competitiveness for alternative products to answer Launchers needs inEurope (and other markers), including if required dual or triple source to limit impacts of specific policy ofeach other,- Physical and chemical characterisation of substitute materials (if no data available) to confirm suitabilitywith launcher requirements.- Make available and regularly update a catalogue of characterised alternative chemicals for Europeanmanufacturers.Deliverables: Other, Report

title: SUPPORT TO THE STANDARDISATION OF THE SATELLITE 6G COMPONENT (ARTES FP 1D.029) EXPRO+
description: The purpose of the activity is to coordinate satcom sector involvement in the 6G standardisation process of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP). The activity scope includes building consensus amongst satcom players, developing contributions to support standardisation actions, and advocating positions favourable to the sector within the standardisation process. The overarching goal being to ensure that the standardisation process results in tangible new opportunities for the satcom industry. In particular, the activity will include support to the Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN)-related work items defined for Release 21 of the 3GPP specification, as well as the preparation of NTN-related items for Release 22 and beyond.

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR LUNAR EXPLORATION (HITLUX) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a high temperature heat transport system for lunar exploration missions, providing an efficientthermal link operating at temperatures in the range of [700degC-1000degC], able to operate within lunarday/night cycles.Description:Sustainable human lunar and planetary exploration relies on effective management of high-temperatureprocesses associated with systems such asIn Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), regenerative fuel cells, andnuclear and chemical heat generation and storage. The temperatures involved are significantly higher than theclassical ranges considered for the design of thermal control subsystems, reaching values of up to 1000degC.In this context, a high-temperature heat transport system is required to ensure effective temperature control through an efficient thermal link operating in the range of [700degC-1000degC]. The developed technology will be compatible with thelunar environment, including potential operational, stand-by and shutdown cycles associated with the lunar day/night periods. As a target, the technology should also be applicable to similar high-temperature systems operating on Mars.This activity aims to develop a breadboard (BB) of a HIgh Temperature heat transport system for LUnareXploration (HITLUX), serving as a technical demonstrator of the feasibility of this technology. The activity is intended to validate the key driving requirements of the system, including anoperating temperature range from 700degC to 1000degC, a heat transport capability up to 700 W over distances of up to 2 m, and withshutdown and start-up capability.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the HITLUX requirements and elaborationof a technical specification- Review of the state of the art- Trade-offs of various housing materials and working fluids and concept definition- Thermal analysis of the proposed solution- Design of the breadboard(s) and the associated test bench(s)- Manufacture of breadboard(s) and test bench(s)- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Thermal model correlation- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further technology maturation and de-risking.

title: POWER EFFICIENT FAST FOURIER TRANSFORM IP CORE - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop and refine a power efficient Fast Fourier Transform IP Core for FPGA/ASIC implementationDescription: This activity focuses on the design, development and testing of a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) block to be used in space applications, which is to be developed as a configurable, reusable IP Core. A reusable IP Core is a hardware model, normally described in VHDL, which is fully verified and can be used as a building block in designs for several targets, such as FPGAs from different vendors or as an ASIC, providing savings in mission costs and development times. The developed IP shall be able to solve complex FFT / inverse FFT; convolve and correlate vectors in frequency domain, with a length up to 32768 points, gain and phase correction, filtering, etc. Several applications will benefit from such an IP Core: - Active Microwave Remote Sensing: Radar Onboard Processing, such as SAR Image Formation, RFI Detection, Compression - Passive Microwave Remote Sensing: Hyperspectral Radiometers (channelisation, RFI detection), Compression Although FFT IPs are available commercially, fine spectral resolution together with high sampling rate (e.g. direct conversion) leads to long FFT lengths, which may not be available in commercial IPs. Furthermore, many of these applications require high-throughput, e.g. channelisation, together with real-time constraints. These requirements give raise to needs regarding adequate standardized Input/Output interfaces (such as AXI-Stream buses) as well as efficient FFT architectures, to cope with the throughput. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Specifications of the FFT IP Core, taking into account the different application needs. - Description of the IP core in VHDL. The IP shall be configurable. - Development of a tool that helps the user configure and generate the IP core based on specific mission requirements. - Verification and Synthesis on relevant space FPGA devices. - Laboratory demonstrator The developed IP core will be offered to future missions and projects as part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, which already includes a catalogue of more than 20 cores which comprise typical digital functions used in space applications (TMTC, EDAC, SpaceWire, CAN, LEON2-FT, OBDH, etc).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
